title: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 02 (Mr. Chips & Advanced Syntax)
subject: english-12

questions.question: In 'The Dying Sun', Sir James Jeans concludes that life most likely originated in:

options.A: Volcanic craters under high electrical discharges
options.B: Lukewarm oceans and shallow pools of water on Earth
options.C: Meteoritic impacts bringing spores from outer galaxies
options.D: High mountain peaks exposed to cosmic rays

questions.explanation: Jeans describes life starting as simple organisms in lukewarm waters, capable of reproducing before dying, slowly evolving into complex beings.

questions.question: What type of student does Dean Hawkes describe as 'the bright boy who has never learned what work is'?

options.A: The student who easily passed high school with minimal effort and finds college standards demanding genuine hard labor.
options.B: The student who has attended night school while working full-time.
options.C: The athlete who refuses to attend lecture halls.
options.D: The student who suffers from chronic organic ailments.

questions.explanation: Students who effortlessly sailed through high school without ever studying often experience shock when college requires consistent, disciplined study.

questions.question: In 'On Destroying Books', J.C. Squire argues that many people hoard bad or useless books because:

options.A: They believe paper will appreciate in commercial value.
options.B: They possess an irrational reverence for printed paper, feeling almost criminal if they throw a book away.
options.C: They intend to build massive private libraries.
options.D: Books are required by law to be preserved for censors.

questions.explanation: People treat printed books with quasi-religious respect, making them reluctant to destroy even worthless poetry or forgotten pamphlets.

questions.question: What was the solitary disease in the medical dictionary that Jerome discovered he did NOT have?

options.A: Gout
options.B: Housemaid's Knee

questions.explanation: He humorously felt slighted and indignant because, out of the entire medical encyclopedia, he did not suffer from 'Housemaid's Knee'.

questions.question: In 'China's Way to Progress', Galeazzo Santini highlights that the Chinese economic miracle was achieved without:

options.A: Massive foreign loans or subservience to western consumerist models
options.B: Hard physical labor by citizens

questions.explanation: China relied on indigenous self-reliance, social discipline, and collective mobilization rather than foreign debt or western capitalist structures.

questions.question: What stark inequality between developed and developing nations is emphasized in 'Hunger and Population'?

options.A: Western citizens consume far more protein and grain, while billions in underdeveloped nations suffer chronic malnutrition and stunted growth.
options.B: Underdeveloped nations have too much food while Europe faces famine.
options.C: Developing nations have no agricultural land.
options.D: Western countries have completely stopped farming.

questions.explanation: Rich countries grapple with obesity and surplus grain, whereas poor countries suffer from severe caloric deficits and child malnutrition.

questions.question: What was the total distance of the trans-Saharan crossing undertaken by Christopher?

options.A: About 3,200 kilometers (2,000 miles) across desert wasteland
options.B: Around 500 kilometers along paved highways

questions.explanation: The Sahara crossing from Algiers to Gao covered over 2,000 miles (3,200 km) of desert sands and scorching rock plateaus.

questions.question: What is the ultimate destination that Christopher reached on the Niger River at the conclusion of his trans-Saharan trek?

options.A: Gao and Timbuktu
options.B: Johannesburg

questions.explanation: Christopher safely navigated the desert and reached Gao on the Niger River, continuing on to ancient Timbuktu.

questions.question: What industrial crisis in France did Pasteur solve by introducing the process that now bears his name (Pasteurization)?

options.A: The spoiling of wine and beer due to unwanted bacterial fermentation
options.B: The explosion of coal mines from methane gas
options.C: The rusting of steel railroad tracks

questions.explanation: Pasteur showed that heating wine and beer to 50–60°C killed harmful microbes without destroying the flavor, saving the French brewing and wine industries.

questions.question: What is the defining biological difference between an antiseptic and an antibiotic?

options.A: Antiseptics are non-specific toxic chemicals used on skin/instruments, whereas antibiotics are biological substances produced by organisms that destroy specific bacteria inside the body without harming host cells.
options.B: Antiseptics cure viral infections while antibiotics cure bacterial diseases.
options.C: Antibiotics are injected into wounds directly while antiseptics are swallowed as tablets.
options.D: There is no difference; they are identical synonyms.

questions.explanation: Antiseptics (e.g. iodine, phenol) destroy living tissue cells indiscriminately; antibiotics (e.g. penicillin) target microbial cell walls without killing human cells.

questions.question: What radical linguistic reform did Mustafa Kemal implement in 1928?

options.A: He replaced the complex Arabic-Persian script with a modified modern Latin alphabet, traveling across Anatolia with a blackboard to teach villagers himself.
options.B: He banned the speaking of Turkish and adopted French.
options.D: He made English the sole medium of instruction in primary schools.

questions.explanation: Kemal introduced the Latin phonetic alphabet, vastly accelerating nationwide literacy; he personally toured towns with a portable blackboard to teach the new letters.

questions.question: What was the psychological impact of Atatürk's educational campaign across Anatolia?

options.A: Literacy skyrocketed as ordinary peasants learned to read and write in months rather than struggling with archaic calligraphy for years.
options.B: Schools were boycotted by parents.

questions.explanation: The simplified Latin script democratized education, unlocking reading, writing, and scientific knowledge for the broad Turkish public.

questions.question: What famous parting words did Katherine whisper to Chips on the eve of their wedding at her aunt's house in London?

options.A: 'Good-bye, Mr. Chips!'
options.B: 'Never look back, Arthur!'

questions.explanation: Teasing him about his formal demeanor and role as a schoolmaster, she whispered playfully: 'Good-bye, Mr. Chips!' giving the novel its famous title.

questions.question: Who was Dr. Merivale, and what routine did he keep with Mr. Chips?

options.A: A friendly local physician who visited Chips every fortnight, told him he was sounder than a bell, and warned him against cold winds
options.B: A rival Latin teacher who plotted against him
options.C: The surgeon general of the army
options.D: A chemist who sold him patent pills

questions.explanation: Dr. Merivale dropped by regularly to monitor Chips' heart, cheerfully declaring that Chips would outlive everyone as long as he stayed warm in winter.

questions.question: How did news of the quarrel between Chips and Ralston leak out to the school?

options.A: A boy waiting in the hallway outside Ralston's study had overheard the raised voices and spread the news like wildfire.
options.B: Ralston published an editorial in the London Times.
options.D: The governors posted notices on the chapel door.

questions.explanation: A student eavesdropping outside the headmaster's door heard the explosive row, igniting a massive wave of student and alumni outrage against Ralston.

questions.question: What was the deeper philosophical meaning of the battle between Chips and Ralston?

options.A: The clash between soulless utilitarian modernity/commercial efficiency and timeless humanistic values, tradition, and personal character
options.B: A dispute over school sports uniforms
options.C: A religious disagreement over chapel hymns

questions.explanation: Hilton frames the clash as a parable of modern mechanical haste colliding with gentle, enduring humanity and tradition.

questions.question: What did Headmaster Cartwright whisper about Chips that prompted the dying old master to open his eyes for the last time?

options.A: 'It's a pity... a great pity he never had any children.'
options.B: 'He was the worst teacher Brookfield ever had.'

questions.explanation: Cartwright whispered that it was sad Chips was a childless bachelor, not knowing of his tragic past with Katherine.

questions.question: What is the tone of the final chapter of 'Good-bye, Mr. Chips'?

options.A: Profoundly moving, serene, nostalgic, and triumphant in its celebration of a life dedicated to youth
options.B: Angry and bitter at the cruelty of death

questions.explanation: The conclusion is filled with spiritual dignity, quiet beauty, and tears of profound fulfillment.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'to leave no stone unturned' mean?

options.A: To do heavy construction work
options.B: To try every possible course of action or exhaust every method to achieve an objective
options.C: To throw rocks into a river
options.D: To search for gemstones in a quarry

questions.explanation: Leaving no stone unturned means exploring every conceivable avenue or strategy to accomplish a goal.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'a feather in one's cap'?

options.A: An achievement or honor of which one can be justly proud
options.B: A bird hunting decoration

questions.explanation: 'A feather in one's cap' is a distinguished achievement or honor that brings credit to someone.
